title: The First Account
dialogue: The note arrived the same way as the first one. Same handwriting. Different three words: Service corridor. Tonight.
monologue: Ten days since the greenhouse. His first report was in the desk drawer exactly where he said it would be. I read it twice. I did not tell Vyktor it existed. I am already in the habit of not telling Vyktor things.

narrative.text: Service Corridor B runs behind the east wing kitchens. It smells of linen and cleaning fluid and the particular institutional cold of spaces that exist only to move things from one place to another. He is standing at the far end, hands in his coat pockets, looking at a wall with the patient attention of a man who finds walls interesting.
Chancellor. There is a matter that requires a decision.
He does not produce a folder. He does not produce anything. He speaks to the wall.

Three weeks ago my people identified a pattern in the Assembly vote records. Four pieces of reform legislation — three failed, one passed in a form that made it functionally useless. The same seven Assembly members voted identically on all four. Bloc voting is not unusual. Paid bloc voting is.

One of the seven — a member from Thornfeld named Caspar Drel — has been receiving payments from a banking entity in Tyvaren. The payments correlate precisely with the four votes. Twelve thousand kroner over eight months, deposited in amounts designed to avoid the reporting threshold. My people have the ledger. They have the transfer records. They have photographs of Drel meeting with the banking entity's Veltrian representative on three occasions.
He turns from the wall. He looks at you with the grey eyes that do not perform anything.
What I do not have is your instruction. That is why I am here.

corridor_arrival.monologue: He has the ledger, the transfer records, and photographs. Three weeks of work I did not authorize because I told him no budget. Except I gave him a budget — or I gave him deniable access to one, or I told him to work within my refusal, and apparently working within my refusal means this. A corrupt Assembly member who has been selling reform votes to Tyvaren for eight months. And a man in a service corridor asking me what to do about it.

choices.text: "I have heard enough. What are my options?"

narrative.text: The labor protection bill in week eight. The banking oversight amendment in week ten. The constitutional committee composition vote in week twelve — that is the significant one. The committee as currently composed will not produce a constitution this government can govern under. Drel's vote was the margin. Tyvaren paid for the committee composition they wanted. They got it.
He says it without anger. He might be describing weather.
Drel is not an ideologue. He is a man with debt and a vote. That makes him manageable in either direction — toward prosecution or toward compliance. Your call.

Three. The first: the ledger goes to Danika Oberlin anonymously. The BCA investigates, prosecutes, Drel is removed from the Assembly. Clean result. The footprint from this operation is minimal — an anonymous tip is standard. You lose the leverage but you gain a precedent.

The second: we keep the ledger. Drel continues voting — but he votes the way you need him to vote. He does not know who holds the ledger. He knows only that someone does and that his career depends on his cooperation. You gain a reliable vote on the constitutional committee. The footprint is moderate.

The third: I arrange a meeting. You and Drel, privately. You show him one page of the ledger. You tell him what you need from the constitutional committee. He understands the conversation without either of you saying anything that can be recorded. Maximum leverage. The footprint from that meeting is significant — two people in a room always leaves more trace than a letter.
He puts his hands back in his coat pockets.

I should tell you something about footprint before you decide. Every operation I run leaves a trace in the world — small, usually invisible, but cumulative. The BCA looks for patterns, not incidents. One anomaly is noise. Twelve anomalies over six months is a pattern. The footprint from this operation is manageable. The next one will cost more. Keep that in mind.

krel_options.monologue: He just named the thing I have been trying not to think about since the greenhouse. Every time I use him, the trace accumulates. Danika looks for patterns. I am building a pattern. The question is whether the leverage I accumulate is worth the pattern I leave — and whether I am the kind of Chancellor who can answer that question honestly.

choices.text: "Send it to Danika. Anonymous tip. Let the BCA do its work. I did not build that agency to work around it."
"Keep the ledger. I want his vote on the constitutional committee. He does not need to know who is holding it over him."
"Arrange the meeting. I want to look at him myself. I want him to understand exactly who is holding his career in their hands."

narrative.text: He nods. One motion, precise.
The tip will reach Danika's office by morning. Formatted to look like it came from within the Assembly — a colleague who noticed the pattern. She will have no reason to look further than Drel.

You lose the leverage on the committee vote. I want you to know that before the BCA investigation closes the option. Once Drel is under investigation, he becomes useless as an instrument. You are choosing accountability over control. That is a coherent choice. It has a cost.
He turns to leave. At the end of the corridor he stops without turning.
The footprint from this operation is three. Running total: eight. Danika's threshold for pattern recognition is approximately forty. We have time.

journalEntry.title: The First Account
journalEntry.content: Krel found a corrupt Assembly member selling reform votes to Tyvaren. I sent the ledger to Danika anonymously. The BCA will handle it. That is what the BCA is for. Krel told me the footprint running total is eight. He is keeping a count. I did not ask him to. He does it anyway.

narrative.text: He says nothing for a moment. He is not surprised. He is confirming.

Understood. The ledger stays with my people. Drel will receive a communication next week — indirect, untraceable — making clear that his voting record on the constitutional committee is being monitored by a party with an interest in his continued discretion. He will understand.
He is not a courageous man. That makes him reliable. Courageous men resist. Men with debt and ambition calculate. He will calculate correctly.
He turns to leave.
The footprint from this operation is eight. Running total: thirteen. Danika's threshold is approximately forty. Keep that in mind when you decide how often to call on me.

journalEntry.title: The First Account
journalEntry.content: A corrupt Assembly member is now voting the way I need him to vote because a man I cannot name is holding a ledger he does not know exists. I told myself it was necessary. The constitutional committee composition matters. The vote matters. I keep telling myself it was necessary. Krel says the footprint running total is thirteen.

narrative.text: Something shifts in his expression. Not approval — recognition. A recalibration of his model.

The meeting will be arranged for next week. A private room at the Ashenmere Library — Drel uses the reading room on Tuesday evenings. My people will ensure you arrive after him and leave before him. There will be no record of the meeting in either schedule.

One instruction for the meeting: do not threaten him explicitly. Show him the page. Tell him you look forward to working together on the constitutional committee. Let him fill in the rest. Explicit threats can be reported. Implications cannot.
He is at the end of the corridor before you realize he has moved.
The footprint from this operation is twelve. Running total: seventeen. I would recommend some restraint before the next one. We are moving faster than I planned.

journalEntry.title: The First Account
journalEntry.content: I met Caspar Drel in a private room at the Ashenmere Library. I showed him one page of the ledger. I told him I looked forward to working together on the constitutional committee. He looked at the page for a long time. Then he said he was honored to serve the Republic. The footprint running total is seventeen. Krel says we are moving faster than he planned. I am not sure that is a warning or a compliment.
